 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread formulaic text reuse within the Pali canon, recording 122 matching passages across 58 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its opening verses closely match another homonymous poem in the collection, the earlier *Daṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 357, segment range §0.2–3.4) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, standard clausal sequences and stock verse blocks (§3.1–8.1) are shared extensively with other *Apadāna* accounts, including the two poems titled *Mañcadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 422 and Tha-Ap 524), *Labujadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 384), and *Ghatamaṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 428 and 498), as well as the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records weak algorithmic alignment with the Tibetan translation of the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155-2), though with a low plausibility score [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
